face-to-face CSEW collection resumed on 4 October 2021; the upper age limit for domestic-abuse sexual-assault and stalking self-completion modules was removed; coverage after the change differs from earlier age-limited series.
age-coverage change creates comparability considerations; post-resumption estimates also depend on interview-month coverage.
the domestic-abuse release combines several data sources; sources use different timescales and reference periods; the datasets do not all count the same thing and cannot be directly compared.
a combined narrative is not a merged metric; source-specific units and populations must remain visible.
year ending March 2022 estimates used six months of face-to-face interviews; the estimates were not accredited official statistics; ONS instructs users to interpret them with caution.
the six-month estimate is not equivalent to a normal 12-month collection; designation must be preserved.
year ending March 2023 estimates used eight months of interviews; October 2022 to January 2023 data were excluded; an error in the survey caused missing data for some respondents.
partial-year estimates require explicit month coverage; the error affects comparability and precision.
new questions entered a split-sample trial from April 2023; the trial concluded in March 2025; from April 2025 the full sample received the new questions.
trial and full-sample phases require different metadata; transition timing can affect annual estimates.

estimates from the new questions cannot be directly compared with estimates from previous questions; ONS does not provide an adjustment that makes the two series directly comparable; year ending March 2024 onwards uses the new measure.
changes must not be described as real-world trends across the break; measure version is mandatory.
outcome 15 requires a named suspect; the victim supports police action; evidential difficulties prevent further action and can include a wanted suspect who cannot be traced.
outcome 15 is not equivalent to no suspect; closure can remain pending further action.
outcome 16 requires a named suspect; the victim does not support or has withdrawn support from police action; it is a victim-based evidential-difficulties category.
non-support must not be interpreted as absence of an offence; outcome 16 differs materially from outcome 15.
outcome 18 applies where no suspect is identified; the crime has been investigated as far as reasonably possible; the case is closed pending further investigative opportunities.
closed does not mean permanently incapable of reopening; outcome 18 is not a safety score.

the cohort method follows offences recorded in a defined period; outcomes accumulate as investigations progress; the method is useful for offence types such as sexual offences that can take longer to close.
recent cohorts are incomplete; rates change as the cohort matures.

the closed-period method counts outcomes recorded in the reporting year; the associated crime may have been recorded in an earlier period; this measure differs from the recorded-offence cohort method.
volumes mix crime cohorts; the two outcome views must not be merged without a bridge.

median days are calculated from record-level Home Office Data Hub data; force coverage can differ by table and offence group; forces with missing or quality-problem data are excluded from specified medians.
median coverage is not uniform across every figure; excluded-force notes must accompany comparisons.
persistent_id is a 64-character crime identifier; the API id is not guaranteed to remain the same for a crime; the API id is not a police identifier.
persistent_id stability does not validate spatial accuracy; identifier fields must not be interchanged.
the endpoint returns crimes that could not be mapped to a location; location and location_type are null and location_subtype is empty; the latest available month is used when date is omitted.
unmapped crimes are not zero crime; mutable latest-month defaults must be pinned.
status-update-unavailable is a documented outcome category; the category is distinct from under-investigation; absence of an update is represented explicitly.
unavailable status is not evidence of no outcome; category and date must be retained separately.
